# Technical Details {#sec-techdetails}

This part gives the full mathematical specification of the `openMSE` modeling framework. Each chapter derives the equations governing one component of the model, defines notation, and documents the assumptions. Cross-references to the relevant conceptual chapters in [Operating Model Concepts](#sec-om-concepts) are provided for readers who want the higher-level description first.

@sec-tech-notation defines the index sets, dimensions, and mathematical conventions used throughout the Technical Details chapters. **This chapter is not complete**.

@sec-tech-populate-om describes how parameter arrays are constructed from the input objects, including how stochastic draws are taken and how conditioning data are incorporated.

@sec-tech-life-history derives growth, maturity, natural mortality, and fecundity-at-age, including the equations for time-varying schedules.

@sec-tech-fleet-schedules covers fishing mortality, selectivity, retention, and discard mortality, including how these vary over time and across simulations.

@sec-tech-unfished derives the unfished equilibrium population, including numbers-at-age, biomass, spawning biomass, and recruitment, which sets the initial conditions for the historical period.

@sec-tech-historical specifies the full age-structured population dynamics over the historical period, including recruitment, mortality, movement, and how initial conditions are set.

@sec-tech-observations describes how the observation model generates fishery data from the true population, including catch and effort, abundance indices, and composition data.

@sec-tech-refpoints gives the full specification of MSY and auxiliary reference point calculations, including the per-recruit framework, fleet allocation, equilibrium recruitment, and seasonal and spatial considerations.

@sec-tech-projection specifies the forward simulation used during the MSE projection period, including how management advice is applied and how data are generated each time step. **This chapter is not complete**.
